mainTopic: Which מצוות apply only in ארץ ישראל, and whether רבי אליעזר is stricter about חדש
overview: This amud opens with the end of the משנה. ערלה and כלאים apply even outside ארץ ישראל, and רבי אליעזר adds חדש. The גמרא first rejects the idea that a 'land-dependent' מצוה is one written with the word 'coming' into the land, because of תפילין and פטר חמור. רב יהודה gives the real rule: a חובת הגוף applies everywhere, while a חובת קרקע applies only in ארץ ישראל. A ברייתא on דברים 12 proves this by comparing to עבודה זרה. The גמרא then asks whether רבי אליעזר's view on חדש is stricter or more lenient than the first תנא, and lays out both readings based on the word 'מושב'. From אביי's statement that רבי ישמעאל, who limits 'מושב' to after settling the land, is the one who argues with רבי אליעזר, it proves that רבי אליעזר is the stricter one. Finally, the גמרא asks which מצוה רבי ישמעאל was talking about, answers נסכים, and starts a question about נסכים that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Exceptions to the land rule: ערלה, כלאים, and maybe חדש
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists exceptions: ערלה and כלאים apply even outside ארץ ישראל. רבי אליעזר adds חדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Except for ערלה and כלאים. רבי אליעזר says: also חדש.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of the משנה. It gives exceptions to its rule that land-based מצוות apply only in ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה just said that any מצוה tied to the land applies only in ארץ ישראל. Here it names land-based מצוות that still apply everywhere: ערלה and כלאים. רבי אליעזר holds that חדש also applies everywhere.

keyTerms.meaning: Fruit of a tree in its first three years, which is forbidden
Forbidden mixtures, here of seeds and plants
New grain, forbidden to eat until the עומר is brought
Except for

steps.confusionAlert: ערלה and כלאים are still land-based מצוות. The משנה is not saying they are body duties. They are exceptions that happen to apply outside ארץ ישראל as well.

phrases.english: Except for orlah and kilayim.
Rabbi Eliezer says: also the new grain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the משנה's rule about land-based מצוות by listing its exceptions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ערלה and כלאים apply outside ארץ ישראל too. רבי אליעזר holds the same for חדש.

steps.title: What counts as 'tied to the land'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a definition of a מצוה that is tied to the land and one that is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is 'dependent' and what is 'not dependent'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts by asking what the משנה means by a מצוה that is 'dependent' on the land. This sets up the next steps, which try out a definition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה used the words תלויה and שאינה תלויה without defining them. The גמרא wants a clear rule for telling which מצוות belong in each group.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion of the משנה
What?
Dependent on, tied to (the land)

phrases.english: Gemara: What is 'dependent'
and what is 'not dependent'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a definition of the משנה's key term.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The definition of a מצוה התלויה בארץ compared to one that is not.

steps.title: The 'coming into the land' definition fails
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that a land-dependent מצוה is one written with the word 'coming' into the land. It rejects this because תפילין and פטר חמור are written with that word, yet they apply everywhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say 'dependent' means the word 'coming' is written about it, and 'not dependent' means the word 'coming' is not written about it, then what about תפילין and פטר חמור? The word 'coming' is written about them, and they apply both in the land and outside the land!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries out a possible definition and immediately knocks it down with a counterexample.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proposal ties 'dependent' to the wording of the פסוק: does it mention coming into the land? תפילין and פטר חמור appear right after 'when ה׳ brings you to the land,' yet everyone agrees they apply everywhere. So the wording test cannot be the real rule.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a proposal about to be rejected)
Coming, being brought (into the land)
But look at (introduces a counterexample)
Firstborn donkey, which must be redeemed with a lamb
Boxes holding פסוקים, worn on the arm and head

phrases.english: If you say 'dependent' means
that 'coming' is written about it,
and 'not dependent' means
that 'coming' is not written about it,
but look at tefillin and the firstborn donkey,
phrases.notes: Both come from שמות 13:11–16, which opens with 'when ה׳ brings you to the land.'

phrases.english: where 'coming' is written about them,
and they apply both in the land
and outside the land!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to the question and refutes it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proposed definition that 'dependent' means the word ביאה is written about the מצוה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תפילין and פטר חמור are written with ביאה, yet they apply everywhere. So the wording test does not match the halacha.

steps.title: רב יהודה: body duty versus land duty
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that the משנה means a חובת הגוף applies everywhere, while a חובת קרקע applies only in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: This is what the משנה means. Any מצוה that is a duty on the body applies both in the land and outside the land. A duty on the land applies only in the land.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives the correct definition. The test is what the מצוה is about, not what words the פסוק uses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test changes from the wording of the פסוק to the nature of the מצוה. A מצוה that obligates the person, like תפילין, goes with the person wherever he is. A מצוה that is about the ground and its produce applies only in ארץ ישראל. This solves the problem raised by תפילין and פטר חמור.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means
A duty on the person's body
A duty connected to the land and its produce
Applies, is in force

steps.whatToRemember: The key line is חובת הגוף (everywhere) versus חובת קרקע (only in ארץ ישראל). It depends on the type of מצוה, not on the words of the פסוק.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic rule used across halacha to decide which מצוות apply outside ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: this is what it means:
any מצוה that is an obligation of the body
applies both in the land
and outside the land;
an obligation of the land
applies only in the land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected definition with a correct one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Dependent' meant that the פסוק mentions coming into the land.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Dependent' means a חובת קרקע. A חובת הגוף applies everywhere.

steps.title: What is the source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where this rule comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of רב יהודה's rule. This sets up the ברייתא that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that the rule is defined, the גמרא wants a פסוק behind it, to show that the difference between land duties and body duties comes from the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things?

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the scriptural basis of רב יהודה's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the rule that land duties apply only in ארץ ישראל and body duties apply everywhere.

steps.title: A ברייתא begins explaining דברים 12:1
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that goes through the words of דברים 12:1 one phrase at a time: חקים are the expositions, משפטים are the laws, 'you shall observe' is learning, and 'to do' is action.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the רבנן taught: 'These are the statutes' means the expositions. 'And the ordinances' means the laws. 'That you shall observe' means learning. 'To do' means action.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins bringing its source, a ברייתא on the פסוק 'these are the statutes.' This step only starts the explanation. The part that proves the rule comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first explains each phrase of the פסוק. It names the kinds of Torah material (expositions and laws) and the two stages of keeping them (learning and doing). Next it will set 'in the land' against 'all the days that you live upon the earth' (step 7). It then settles the matter by comparing to עבודה זרה in the next פסוק (step 8).

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן taught (introduces a ברייתא)
Statutes
Expositions learned from the פסוקים
Ordinances; here, laws between people
Action, actually doing the מצוה

steps.confusionAlert: Here the word משנה does not mean the book of משנה. It means learning or study.

phrases.english: As the Sages taught:
'These are the statutes': these are the expositions.
'And the ordinances': these are the laws.
'That you shall observe': this is study.
'To do': this is action.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the request for a source by quoting a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that land duties apply only in ארץ ישראל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא explaining דברים 12:1, which continues in steps 7 and 8.

steps.title: Two phrases in the verse seem to pull in opposite directions
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא shows that 'in the land' suggests the מצוות apply only in ארץ ישראל, while 'all the days that you live upon the earth' suggests they apply everywhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: From 'in the land' you might think all the מצוות apply only in ארץ ישראל. So the פסוק says 'all the days that you live upon the earth.' But from 'all the days' you might think they all apply both in ארץ ישראל and outside it. So the פסוק says 'in the land.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues going through the פסוק. It points out that two phrases in it seem to point in opposite directions, and it is setting up how it will resolve that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'In the land' alone would limit every מצוה to ארץ ישראל. 'All the days that you live' alone would make every מצוה apply everywhere. Since the פסוק has both, some מצוות must apply everywhere and some only in the land, and the next step explains which are which.

keyTerms.meaning: 'One might think': introduces a mistaken idea the פסוק then corrects
'The verse teaches': introduces the words of the פסוק that answer the mistaken idea
In the land, meaning ארץ ישראל
Outside ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: "In the land": one might think
that all the מצוות, every one of them,
apply only in the land?
So the verse teaches:

phrases.aramaic: ״כׇּל הַיָּמִים אֲשֶׁר אַתֶּם חַיִּים עַל הָאֲדָמָה״.
phrases.english: "All the days that you live upon the earth."
phrases.notes: Same פסוק, דברים 12:1. The point is: wherever you live.

phrases.english: If it said only "all the days,"
one might think they all apply
both in the land and outside the land?
So the verse teaches: "in the land."

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל כׇּל הַמִּצְוֹת כּוּלָּן לֹא יְהוּ נוֹהֲגִים אֶלָּא בָּאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from step 6, moving on to the last phrases of the same פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That some מצוות apply everywhere and some only in ארץ ישראל
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא on דברים 12:1: 'in the land' versus 'all the days that you live upon the earth'

steps.title: Learning from idol worship: a duty on the person applies everywhere
steps.stepSummary: Since the פסוק both includes and excludes, the ברייתא learns from עבודה זרה in the next פסוק: every חובת הגוף applies both in and outside the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the פסוק both included and excluded, go learn from what is said in the passage: 'You shall destroy all the places where they served...' Just as עבודה זרה is special in that it is a duty on the person and applies both in and outside the land, so too every duty on the person applies both in and outside the land.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא settles the tension from step 7 by comparing to עבודה זרה, which appears in the very next פסוק. This finishes the source for רב יהודה's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עבודה זרה is a clear case of a חובת הגוף, and everyone agrees it is forbidden everywhere. So every חובת הגוף follows it and applies everywhere. That leaves the 'in the land' limit for מצוות tied to the soil, the חובת קרקע.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק 'included' (made it wider) and 'excluded' (made it narrower)
'Go and learn': learn the answer from another place
Idol worship
Special or distinct: the feature that marks this case

steps.whatToRemember: חובת הגוף (a duty on the person) applies everywhere, just like עבודה זרה. חובת קרקע (a duty tied to the land) applies only in ארץ ישראל. This is the source for רב יהודה's rule in step 4.
steps.whyThisMatters: This comparison is the basic rule for which מצוות a Jew keeps outside ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: Since the verse included and also excluded,
go and learn from what is said in the same passage:
"You shall surely destroy all the places
where they served, etc."
Just as idol worship is special
in that it is a duty on the person,

phrases.aramaic: וְנוֹהֶגֶת בֵּין בָּאָרֶץ בֵּין בְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ –
phrases.english: and it applies both in the land and outside the land,
so too, anything that is a duty on the person

phrases.aramaic: נוֹהֶגֶת בֵּין בָּאָרֶץ בֵּין בְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ.
phrases.english: applies both in the land and outside the land.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַחַר שֶׁרִיבָּה הַכָּתוּב וּמִיעֵט צֵא וּלְמַד מִמַּה שֶּׁאָמוּר בָּעִנְיָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the tension between the two phrases raised in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's rule that חובת הגוף applies everywhere and חובת קרקע only in the land
steps.raayaSupportSource: Comparison to עבודה זרה in דברים 12:2
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Every חובת הגוף applies both in and outside ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: Is רבי אליעזר being stricter or more lenient?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's exceptions, ערלה and כלאים, and asks whether רבי אליעזר's disagreement makes the law stricter or more lenient.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'except for ערלה and כלאים.' A question was asked: does רבי אליעזר disagree in order to be lenient, or in order to be strict?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a new line of the משנה, the two exceptions that apply even outside the land. It asks how to understand רבי אליעזר's disagreement there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי אליעזר adds חדש (the new grain) to this discussion. The question is whether his view makes חדש apply in more places than the first view does (stricter) or in fewer places (more lenient).

keyTerms.meaning: Fruit of a tree in its first three years, which may not be eaten
Forbidden mixtures of seeds or plants
'A question was asked before them': opens a real question that needs to be worked out
To be lenient / to be strict
He disagrees

phrases.english: "Except for orla and diverse kinds."
A question was asked before them:
Does Rabbi Eliezer disagree to be lenient,
or does he disagree to be strict?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לְקוּלָּא פְּלִיג אוֹ לְחוּמְרָא פְּלִיג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the exceptions in the משנה, after the general rule was proven in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which way רבי אליעזר's disagreement goes regarding חדש outside the land

steps.title: The stricter reading: the first view limits חדש to the land
steps.stepSummary: If רבי אליעזר is stricter, then the first view holds that only ערלה and כלאים apply outside the land, through a received tradition, while חדש applies only in the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: He disagrees to be strict. And this is what the first view says: except for ערלה and כלאים, which we know through a received tradition, even though one could say each is a duty tied to the land. But חדש: in the land, yes; outside the land, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the first side of the question would mean. If רבי אליעזר is the strict one, the first view must be saying that חדש does not apply outside the land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the general rule, ערלה and כלאים are duties tied to the land and should apply only in ארץ ישראל. They apply outside it only because of a special tradition. חדש has no such tradition, so on this reading the first view keeps it in ארץ ישראל, and רבי אליעזר is stricter by saying it applies outside too.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed view in the משנה
'We learned it as a received law': a tradition from משה at סיני
A duty tied to the land
New grain, which may not be eaten before the עומר is brought

steps.confusionAlert: This is only ONE side of the question. Here the גמרא is only showing what the first view would mean if רבי אליעזר were the strict one. It decides between the two readings in steps 16 to 20.

phrases.english: He disagrees to be strict,
and this is what the first Tanna is saying:
except for orla and diverse kinds,
which we learned as a received law,
phrases.notes: A tradition handed down from משה at סיני, not something learned from a פסוק.

phrases.english: even though one could say
that it is a duty tied to the land.
But new grain:
in the land, yes;
outside the land, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְחוּמְרָא פְּלִיג וְהָכִי קָאָמַר תַּנָּא קַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the first possibility of the question raised in step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: On the strict reading, the first view holds that חדש applies only in ארץ ישראל, and only ערלה and כלאים apply outside it through tradition. רבי אליעזר then adds חדש outside the land.

steps.title: Why the first תנא says חדש applies only in the land
steps.stepSummary: In the stricter reading, the first תנא reads 'מושב' (dwelling) as the time after the Jews conquered and settled ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? The word 'dwelling' means after inheriting and settling the land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still building the first reading, where רבי אליעזר is stricter. Here it gives the reason the first תנא limits חדש to ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about חדש says 'בכל מושבותיכם', 'in all your dwellings'. The first תנא reads 'dwelling' as settled life in the land after it was conquered. So the word ties חדש to ארץ ישראל, not to wherever Jews live.

keyTerms.meaning: Dwelling; the key word in the פסוק about חדש
Inheritance, meaning conquering the land
Settling in the land
It implies; this is how the word reads

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: The reason of the first תנא, who says חדש applies only in the land.

phrases.english: "Dwelling" means after inheritance
and settlement, that is what it implies.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא? ״מוֹשָׁב״ – לְאַחַר יְרוּשָּׁה וִישִׁיבָה מַשְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind the first תנא's view as laid out in Step 10's stricter reading.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first תנא reads 'מושב' as after conquest and settlement, so חדש is limited to ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: In the stricter reading, רבי אליעזר says חדש applies everywhere
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר adds חדש to the list of things that apply outside the land, because he reads 'מושב' as wherever you live.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר comes to say: even חדש applies both in the land and outside it. Why? 'Dwelling' means wherever you dwell.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the stricter reading. רבי אליעזר's 'אף' (even) adds חדש to ערלה and כלאים as things that apply outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole argument is about one word. The first תנא reads 'מושב' as settlement in the land, but רבי אליעזר reads it as any place Jews live. That makes רבי אליעזר stricter, since חדש is forbidden everywhere.

keyTerms.meaning: Even, also; adding something to a list
Applies, is in force
Outside ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer comes to say:
Even the new crop applies
both in the land and outside the land.
What is the reason? "Dwelling"
means in every place where you dwell.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲתָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לְמֵימַר: אַף חָדָשׁ נוֹהֵג בֵּין בָּאָרֶץ בֵּין בְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the stricter reading by giving רבי אליעזר's opposing view and his reason.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In the stricter reading, רבי אליעזר holds חדש applies everywhere because 'מושב' means wherever you live.

steps.title: In the lenient reading, the first תנא says חדש applies everywhere
steps.stepSummary: Maybe רבי אליעזר is more lenient. Then the first תנא held that ערלה and כלאים apply outside the land, and חדש even more surely does.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps he disagrees to be lenient. Then the first תנא is saying: except for ערלה and כלאים, which are a received tradition, and all the more so חדש, since 'dwelling' means wherever you dwell.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers the second way to read the משנה, where רבי אליעזר is the lenient one. In this reading, the first תנא already includes חדש outside the land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the two readings of 'מושב' switch sides. Now the first תנא reads it as 'wherever you dwell'. ערלה and כלאים outside the land rest only on a received tradition, while חדש has a פסוק saying it directly. So the first תנא did not need to mention חדש, because it applies 'all the more so'.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps; introduces a second way to read it
To be lenient
He disagrees
They learned it as a received law (a tradition)
All the more so

steps.confusionAlert: Both readings use the same two ways of reading 'מושב'. They just switch which side holds which. In this reading the first תנא is the strict one.

phrases.english: Or perhaps he disagrees in order to be lenient,
and this is what the first Tanna is saying:
except for orla and diverse kinds,
which they learned as a received law,
and all the more so the new crop,
since "dwelling" means every place
where you dwell; that is what it implies.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ דִלְמָא לְקוּלָּא פְּלִיג, וְהָכִי קָאָמַר תַּנָּא קַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the second option from Step 9's question, reversing the reading of Steps 10-12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In the lenient reading, the first תנא holds חדש applies everywhere, even more surely than ערלה and כלאים.

steps.title: In the lenient reading, רבי אליעזר says חדש applies only in the land
steps.stepSummary: In this reading, רבי אליעזר limits חדש to ארץ ישראל, reading 'מושב' as after conquest and settlement.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר comes to say: חדש applies only in the land, because 'dwelling' means after inheriting and settling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the lenient reading by giving רבי אליעזר's view. He holds that חדש outside the land is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is exactly the reading the first תנא used in Step 11, now put in רבי אליעזר's mouth. So in this version, רבי אליעזר is the lenient one.

keyTerms.meaning: Applies only in ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer comes to say:
the new crop applies only in the land,
since "dwelling" means after inheritance
and settlement; that is what it implies.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲתָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לְמֵימַר: חָדָשׁ אֵינוֹ נוֹהֵג אֶלָּא בָּאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the lenient reading begun in Step 13 by giving רבי אליעזר's side.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In the lenient reading, רבי אליעזר holds חדש is limited to ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: What 'even' means in the lenient reading
steps.stepSummary: If רבי אליעזר is lenient, his word 'אף' points back to the first part of the משנה‎: מצוות tied to the land apply only in the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what does 'even' mean? It refers to the first part.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a problem with the lenient reading. If רבי אליעזר is not adding חדש to ערלה and כלאים, what is his word 'even' adding to?
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אף' does not attach to ערלה and כלאים. It attaches to the opening rule of the משנה, that מצוות tied to the land apply only in the land. רבי אליעזר is saying that חדש also belongs under that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: On the first one; the first part of the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה can be read two ways. In the stricter reading, the first תנא limits חדש to the land, and רבי אליעזר says 'even חדש' applies everywhere. In the lenient reading, the first תנא says חדש applies everywhere, all the more so than ערלה and כלאים, and רבי אליעזר limits it to the land, with 'even' pointing back to the משנה's opening rule. Both readings depend on how you read 'מושב'.

phrases.english: And what is the meaning of "even"?
It refers to the first part.
phrases.notes: The first part of the משנה: a מצוה tied to the land applies only in the land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves a wording problem that the lenient reading of Steps 13-14 creates.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading which clause the word 'אף' attaches to
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'אף' seems to add חדש to ערלה and כלאים, which apply outside the land, and that would only fit the stricter reading.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אף' attaches to the opening rule, that מצוות tied to the land apply only in the land, so it fits the lenient reading too.

steps.title: אביי names the תנא who argues with רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a proof from אביי, who says that the תנא who argues with רבי אליעזר is רבי ישמעאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear a proof from what אביי said: Who is the תנא who argues with רבי אליעזר? It is רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a proof to decide which reading of רבי אליעזר is correct, stricter or more lenient. It starts with אביי's statement that רבי ישמעאל is the one who argues with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By itself, this line does not prove anything yet. Once we see what רבי ישמעאל holds about 'מושב', we will know what the opposing side (רבי אליעזר) must hold.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the גמרא is bringing a proof
אביי, a major אמורא
Who is the תנא (the teacher of the משנה period)?
Who argues with him

phrases.english: Come and hear, for אביי said:

phrases.aramaic: מַאן תַּנָּא דִּפְלִיג עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר –
phrases.english: Who is the תנא who argues with רבי אליעזר?
It is רבי ישמעאל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the two possible readings of רבי אליעזר were laid out, the גמרא now tries to prove which reading is right.
steps.raayaObject: Which reading of רבי אליעזר is correct: stricter or more lenient.
steps.raayaSupportSource: אביי's statement that רבי ישמעאל is the one who argues with רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: 'מושב' means after conquering and settling the land
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי ישמעאל: wherever the Torah says 'מושב', the מצוה applies only after the Jews conquered and settled the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: This comes to teach you that any place where the word 'dwelling' is written, the מצוה applies only after the land was inherited and settled. These are the words of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא to show what רבי ישמעאל holds: the word 'מושב' ties a מצוה to the time after conquest and settlement of ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the reading of 'מושב' that limits a מצוה to ארץ ישראל, the same one the first תנא used in step 11. If רבי ישמעאל reads 'מושב' this way, the one he argues with, רבי אליעזר, must read it as 'wherever you live'.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
Dwelling, a word the Torah uses in some מצוות
Inheriting (conquering) and settling the land

phrases.english: As it was taught: This comes to teach you
that any place where 'dwelling' is said
it applies only after inheriting and settling the land,
these are the words of רבי ישמעאל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows what רבי ישמעאל, named by אביי, actually holds.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wherever the Torah says 'מושב', the מצוה applies only after the land was conquered and settled.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא challenges from שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא asks: the Torah says 'מושבות' about שבת, yet שבת applies everywhere, both in the land and outside it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said to him: But look at שבת. The Torah says 'dwellings' about it, and it applies both in the land and outside the land!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא attacks רבי ישמעאל's rule with a counterexample: שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'מושב' always ties a מצוה to the land after settlement, then שבת should only apply in ארץ ישראל. But everyone agrees שבת applies everywhere, so the rule seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי עקיבא, a great תנא
But look at שבת: a counterexample
Outside ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: רבי עקיבא said to him:
But look at שבת, where 'dwellings' is said,

phrases.aramaic: וְנוֹהֶגֶת בֵּין בָּאָרֶץ בֵּין בְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ!
phrases.english: and it applies both in the land and outside the land!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: הֲרֵי שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule רבי ישמעאל just stated.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל's rule that 'מושב' always means after conquest and settlement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שבת uses the word 'מושבות' but applies everywhere, so the word cannot always limit a מצוה to the land.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: שבת comes from a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל answers that שבת applies everywhere because of a קל וחומר, not because of the word 'מושבות'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: שבת comes from a קל וחומר. If lighter מצוות apply both in the land and outside the land, then שבת, which is serious, surely does!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל defends his rule by explaining that שבת gets its 'everywhere' status from a different source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'מושבות' alone would limit שבת to the land. But a קל וחומר from lighter מצוות that apply everywhere shows that the very serious שבת must apply everywhere too, so his rule about 'מושב' still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'how much more so' argument, from a lighter case to a more serious one
Lighter, less serious מצוות
Serious, strict
All the more so, surely

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: שַׁבָּת קַל וָחוֹמֶר אָתְיָא,
phrases.english: He said to him: שבת comes from a קל וחומר,
if light מצוות apply
both in the land and outside the land,
then שבת, which is serious, all the more so!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: שַׁבָּת קַל וָחוֹמֶר אָתְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי עקיבא's challenge from שבת.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different source: the law comes from a קל וחומר, not from the word 'מושבות'.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שבת uses 'מושבות' and applies everywhere, so 'מושב' cannot mean only in the land.
steps.terutzMaskana: שבת applies everywhere because of a קל וחומר; the rule that 'מושב' means after settlement still holds.

steps.title: So רבי אליעזר is the stricter one
steps.stepSummary: Since אביי says רבי ישמעאל argues with רבי אליעזר, and רבי ישמעאל limits 'מושב' to the land, רבי אליעזר must be arguing to be stricter.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since אביי said that the תנא who argues with רבי אליעזר is רבי ישמעאל, learn from this that רבי אליעזר argues to be stricter. Yes, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof: רבי אליעזר holds the stricter view, that חדש applies outside the land too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל reads 'מושב' as after settlement, which limits a מצוה to the land. The one he argues with, רבי אליעזר, must read 'מושב' as wherever you live, which makes חדש apply everywhere. This confirms the stricter reading from step 12 and rejects the lenient reading of steps 13 to 15.

keyTerms.meaning: Since he said
Learn from this; also used to confirm a conclusion
He argues to be stricter

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר is stricter: he holds that חדש applies even outside ארץ ישראל, because he reads 'מושב' as wherever you live. רבי ישמעאל is the one who argues with him.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי ישמעאל is not the stricter one here. He limits 'מושב' to the land. That is exactly why the one he argues with, רבי אליעזר, comes out stricter.

phrases.english: Since אביי said:

phrases.aramaic: מַאן תַּנָּא דִּפְלִיג עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר –
phrases.english: Who is the תנא who argues with רבי אליעזר?
It is רבי ישמעאל,

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לְחוּמְרָא פְּלִיג,
phrases.english: learn from this that רבי אליעזר argues to be stricter,
yes, learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי ישמעאל's view from steps 17 to 19 to finish the proof begun in step 16.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי אליעזר argues to be stricter: חדש applies outside the land as well.

steps.title: Which מצוה was רבי ישמעאל talking about? נסכים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks a side question: which מצוה was רבי ישמעאל's teaching about? The answer is נסכים (wine offerings). Then it begins a new question about נסכים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, what was רבי ישמעאל talking about? About נסכים. About נסכים...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a side discussion to find which מצוה רבי ישמעאל's ברייתא was about, and answers: נסכים. The last word sets up the next question, which continues further on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל's rule was taught on a specific פסוק that uses 'מושב'. Knowing it was about נסכים lets the גמרא go on to ask about how his rule fits that מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, let us see: opens a new question
Where is he standing? What is he talking about?
Wine offerings poured with קרבנות

phrases.english: Now, what was רבי ישמעאל talking about?
About נסכים.
About נסכים...

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the proof, the גמרא turns to a side question about the context of רבי ישמעאל's ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which מצוה רבי ישמעאל's teaching about 'מושב' was based on.
